title: Semantic preservation harness for OpenAI ChatCompletions request/response mapping
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: implement a mapping layer that translates OpenAI Chat Completions (OA-CC) requests and streaming/responses into Redwood's internal API with minimal semantic loss. This ticket focuses on the hard edge cases: partial/streamed JSON content for structured outputs, function/tool call signals expressed mid-stream, role/delta framing differences, and deterministic vs. best-effort function arguments. The harness should provide: (1) deterministic reconstruction of streamed outputs with sequence markers, (2) preservation of function_call metadata (name, arguments, provenance), (3) consistent handling of truncated or broken JSON in partial chunks, and (4) clear telemetry events to detect fidelity regressions.
acceptance_criteria: OA-CC request -> Redwood request mapping preserves message roles, names, and user metadata.
Streamed responses can be reassembled into a single coherent message without semantic drift in 99.9% of synthetic test cases.
Function/tool calls emitted by OA-CC are surfaced as Redwood structured function_call objects with original argument text and a parsed JSON fallback when available.
Backward-compatibility: legacy clients that expect OA streaming frames continue to receive equivalent frames through the compatibility shim when enabled.
Automated regression tests and telemetry for token-level divergences are added and passing in CI.
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after spike investigating mismatches between OA streaming frames and Redwood structured output parsing.
2025-02-21: Prototype implemented that adds sequence_id and final_chunk flags to reassembly buffer; initial tests show 0.6% JSON reassembly failures on adversarial truncation inputs.
2025-02-26: Design review with PM and DX — decided to keep original OA payloads in telemetry for debugging and add an opt-in lenient_json_parser for malformed arguments.
2025-03-01: PoC extended to capture function_call provenance header (source_stream_offset + chunk_index); performance overhead measured at +1.8% p99 latency under 100RPS.
2025-03-04: Merged small refactor to the streaming frame decoder; next: implement acceptance tests and a GitHub PR for the mapping harness.
comments: PM (Lena Ortiz): Focus on observable failure modes customers will see; add a dashboard for streamed vs. reconstructed delta mismatches.
Design (Marco Bianchi): UX should avoid surfacing partial JSON to end users; prefer 'pending' intermediate states and only emit fully reconstructed structured outputs.
Eng Review (Sofia Martinez): We should version the mapping behavior behind a config flag (oa_cc_compat_v2) to allow controlled rollout to Dedicated/Private clusters.
QA (Devon Blake): Add fuzz tests that inject byte-level truncation and shuffled chunk delivery to validate reassembly resilience.
qa_checks: Unit tests for frame reordering and duplicate chunk suppression
Integration test: OA streaming session with interleaved function_call frames -> final structured function_call object
Load test: verify p99 latency and memory usage with 1000 concurrent streaming connections
Fuzz regression: 10k randomized truncation cases must pass or be classified as graceful degradation
design_decisions: Choose explicit chunk metadata (sequence_id, chunk_index, final_chunk) instead of relying on TCP boundaries to reconstruct messages.
Preserve original OA raw delta fragments in an internal debug blob to support post-mortem and customer support requests.
Expose a conservative parser that tries strict JSON parsing first and then falls back to lenient extraction when a function_call argument is syntactically broken.
Roll out mapping behind oa_cc_compat_v2 flag with canary on hosted, then dedicated, then private deployments to reduce blast radius.
